turns.prompt_text: how do I use this Attached 1 file. - 9343f988-0450-4d63-9014-2496261f046d
turns.response_html:
Based on the image you provided, you have a Wall Lenk Solderpro 25 (LSP-25) butane-powered 2-in-1 tool. This device functions as both a cordless soldering iron and a small blow torch.

1. Filling it with Fuel

Before using it, the tool must be filled with butane gas.

  • Safety: Ensure you are in a well-ventilated area away from any open flames or sparks.
  • Fill Port: Locate the small fill valve at the very bottom of the orange handle.
  • Filling: Turn the tool upside down. Insert the nozzle of a butane fuel canister vertically into the valve and press down firmly for about 10 seconds.
  • Stabilize: Let the tool sit for 2–3 minutes after filling to allow the fuel to stabilize and reach room temperature before igniting.

2. Operating the Tool

This model is typically a manual-ignition tool, though some variations have built-in piezo igniters.

  • Ignition: Move the gas adjustment slider (the small black lever often found near the top of the handle) to a middle setting.
  • Flame: Once the gas is flowing, you may need to use a standard lighter near the tip to ignite it if it does not have a self-igniter.
  • Soldering vs. Torch Mode: * Soldering: Keep the metal tip attached. It will take about 10–12 seconds to reach soldering temperature.
    • Torch: To use it as a blow torch for tasks like shrink tubing or thawing locks, you typically unscrew the soldering tip and tip holder to expose the open flame.

3. Safety & Maintenance

  • Avoid Overheating: Do not use the tool continuously for more than one minute without letting it cool for several minutes, as this can damage the internal catalyst or tip.
  • Storage: Always allow the tip to cool completely to room temperature before storing it.
  • Tinning the Tip: To keep the soldering tip in good condition, "tin" it by applying a small amount of solder to the tip as soon as it gets hot for the first time.

turns.response_html:
Since you have identified the fuel (butane), the next step is to ignite and prep the tool for use. Based on your sticky notes about lockpicking and schematics, this tool will be a great addition to your technical kit for heat-shrinking or minor electrical repairs.

Step 1: Ignition

The Wall Lenk LSP-25 features a Piezo electronic automatic ignition system, so you don't need matches.

  1. Open the Gas: Move the gas adjustment slider (the small black lever) to a middle or high setting. You should hear a faint "hissing" sound of the gas escaping.
  2. Ignite: Press the red ignition button firmly until you hear a click.
  3. Check for Heat: Look through the small "viewing hole" on the side of the metal barrel. You should see a internal ceramic catalyst begin to glow orange or red. This means it is successfully lit and heating up.

Step 2: Prepping the Tip ("Tinning")

If you are using the soldering tip for the first time, you must "tin" it to prevent oxidation.

  1. Wait: Give the tool about 25 seconds to reach operating temperature.
  2. Apply Solder: Touch a small amount of rosin-core solder to the very end of the tip. It should melt and coat the tip in a shiny, silver layer.
  3. Wipe: Gently wipe the tip on a damp sponge or brass wire cleaner to remove excess.

Step 3: Usage Modes

  • For Soldering: Use the pointed tip as you would a standard iron. It provides heat equivalent to a 25W to 50W electric iron.
  • For Heat Shrink/Torch: If you need an open flame (for example, to heat a stubborn lock or shrink tubing), you can unscrew the soldering tip to use the tool as a micro-torch. The torch mode reaches much higher temperatures—up to 2400°F.

Important Warnings

  • The Exhaust Port: Be careful of the small hole on the side of the metal barrel; extremely hot air (exhaust) blasts out of here during use. Never point this toward your hand or flammable materials.
  • Shut Down: When finished, slide the gas adjustment lever to the OFF position.
  • Cooling: This tool stays hot for several minutes after being turned off. Wait for it to cool completely before putting the protective cap back on or storing it.
